task.title: Your first stylesheet
task.shortdesc: CSSMedia takes two files: an XML document and a CSS stylesheet. XML contains the document’s elements and text. CSS contains rules that describe how selected elements should be styled.

stepxmp.pre:
Using the device

Follow these steps before starting.

info.p: The names chapter, title, and p belong to this XML document. They are not special CSS names. You can use the names from your own XML in a stylesheet.
A CSS rule has a selector and a declaration block:
The selector title chooses XML elements with that name. The declaration font-size: 18pt; sets a property to a value. The braces contain the declarations for the selected elements.
You can add more declarations to the same rule:

Each declaration has a property name, a colon, a value, and a semicolon. CSSMedia checks property values against the CSS syntax it supports. A selector only matches when it describes elements in your XML.

step.cmd: Use names from your own XML

info.p: The element names in the examples are placeholders. If your XML uses heading instead of title, write heading as the selector:
CSSMedia does not infer that heading is a title or that p is a paragraph. You decide which XML names to select and which CSS properties to set.
Save the XML as document.xml and the stylesheet as document.css, then run CSSMedia:
Open document.pdf. The title element is styled by the rule you wrote.
